findings.issue_text: [BUG] `require 'ruby-readability'` raises LoadError because the ruby-readability gem's library file is `readability.rb`, not `ruby-readability.rb`. TopicEmbed.import_remote (and therefore the embed retrieval job and the disqus thor import) crashes with LoadError on the first call, so no topic is ever retrieved for any embedded URL.

[BUG] `i.content` returns nil for RSS 2.0 feeds (SimpleRSS exposes `content` only for Atom entries), so `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError on nil. For any plain RSS (non-Atom) feed, the hourly PollFeed job crashes mid-iteration with NoMethodError on nil.scrub, and since sidekiq_options retry: false, no posts from that feed are ever imported.

[BUG] String#scrub does not exist on Ruby 2.0, which this codebase's Gemfile_rails4.lock-era Discourse installs run on (scrub was added in Ruby 2.1). On the supported Ruby version, every feed poll raises NoMethodError (undefined method `scrub' for String) after the network fetch succeeds, so feed importing never works and the hourly job fails on every run.

[BUG] ruby-readability and simple-rss are added to the Gemfile but only Gemfile_rails4.lock is updated in this diff; the primary lockfile is not, so `bundle install --deployment`/CI on the main bundle cannot resolve the new dependencies. CI and production deploys fail with 'ruby-readability (>= 0) not found in any of the sources' (Bundler::GemNotFound), blocking the entire build until the lockfile is regenerated and committed.

[BUG] The `best` action calls `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` but when `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), ...)` runs with an anonymous visitor (current_user nil), the enqueued job's `args[:user_id]` is nil, and RetrieveTopic then calls `TopicRetriever.new(embed_url, no_throttle: user.try(:staff?))` with `no_throttle: nil`, so the throttle applies — fine — but the controller renders 'loading' with no @topic_view while the loading view's layout postMessage targets `<%= request.referer %>` which is nil when the referer was absent, emitting `parent.postMessage(..., '')`. Browsers throw a SyntaxError (invalid targetOrigin '') in the embed iframe on every load where request.referer is nil, so the resize postMessage never fires and the embedded iframe stays at default height.

[BUG] `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` executes the entire feed poll synchronously inside the retrieve_topic sidekiq job, but PollFeed's execute guard re-checks `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` — already true — and `poll_feed` then does a blocking `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` network fetch plus a PostCreator DB write per item, all inside a job whose sole purpose is to fetch one URL. Each first-time embed request triggers a full-feed import inside the retrieve_topic worker; a large feed makes the worker block for minutes and hammers the third-party feed server on every new embedded URL, and if the feed fetch raises (e.g. timeout) the RetrieveTopic job fails with retry instead of falling through to fetch_http.

[BUG] TopicEmbed.import stores remote feed/retrieved HTML as cooked content with cook_method raw_html, bypassing the sanitizing cook pipeline, and best.html.erb renders it with raw post.cooked, so any script/iframe injected into the source RSS feed or embedded page executes in the Discourse-origin embed iframe. A compromised or malicious embedded site feeds arbitrary HTML through import_remote/PollFeed; it is rendered unsanitized at /embed/best, giving an attacker script execution in the forum's origin (cookie/CSRF theft) — the normal cook pipeline's sanitization is the control this diff explicitly skips.

[BUG] poll_feed calls CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) and SimpleRSS returns nil for tags absent from an RSS item (RSS items have description, not content), so every poll of a plain RSS feed raises NoMethodError on nil.scrub and no item is ever imported. The hourly PollFeed job crashes on RSS feeds lacking atom:content on every run; feed polling silently produces zero topics and the failure is invisible because retry: false discards the exception.

[BUG] create_table :topic_embeds, force: true drops any pre-existing topic_embeds table (and it also silently drops table data on any environment where the migration re-runs against an existing table), and the same force: true is newly added to create_top_topics in this diff. Running the migration on a database that already has topic_embeds (e.g. a partially migrated environment or redump) destroys the embed mapping rows and topics become orphaned from their embed URLs with no backfill path.

[ADVISORY] The postMessage origin gate uses discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1, a substring containment check rather than exact scheme+host+port equality. Any origin whose string contains the Discourse URL (e.g. http://discourse.example.com.evil.com or a page named after the URL) passes the check and can drive the iframe's height; low impact but trivially fixable by comparing e.origin to a precomputed origin.

[ADVISORY] The loading view blindly reloads every 30 seconds forever, and the controller has no path that ever signals failure: if RetrieveTopic bails (blank embed_by_username, embed_url absent from the feed, readability returns nil, host mismatch between the referer-checked request and the embed_url), the visitor's page re-fetches /embed/best indefinitely. Embedding site visitors see an eternal 'Loading Discussion...' panel and each browser polls the Discourse server every 30 seconds; there is no error state, cap on retries, or user-visible failure.

[ADVISORY] perform_retrieve runs the entire feed poll synchronously via Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) inside the Sidekiq worker instead of enqueuing it, so a worker retrieving one embed URL blocks on opening and parsing the whole remote feed plus readability fetches. A slow/hung feed_polling_url stalls the Sidekiq worker for the full HTTP timeout on every first-time embed hit, degrading all background job throughput for sites with embedding enabled.

[ADVISORY] feed_key is defined (with a comment-implied purpose of conditional fetching via If-Modified-Since) but is never read anywhere in the diff, so every hourly run re-downloads and re-parses the full feed. Dead code that misleads the next maintainer into believing modified-time throttling exists; the actual behavior is a full unthrottled fetch every hour against the source site.

[ADVISORY] absolutize_urls only rewrites href/src values that start with '/', leaving protocol-relative URLs (//host/path), which are common in RSS/Atom content, and bare relative paths (page.html) untouched. Imported articles containing //cdn.example.com/img.png or page-relative links render broken links/images in the embed and the imported topic, and the feed-import path never exercises these in tests.

[ADVISORY] The new non-trivial logic in this diff — TopicEmbed.import_remote (readability extraction), TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve/fetch_http, the Post#cook raw_html branch, and PostCreator's cook_method option — has no test anywhere in the diff; the three specs added only cover import(), retrieve()'s throttle/host gate, and the controller's routing. A regression in the readability fetch path or the cook short-circuit (e.g. raw_html posts silently skipping Plugin::Filter :after_post_cook, which the code at app/models/post.rb:131-134 does for every raw_html post, including legit plugin consumers of that hook) would ship undetected.

[ADVISORY] When a TopicEmbed row exists but its topic has been deleted (TopicEmbed rows are never destroyed with their topic — no dependent hook or deletion path exists in the diff), topic_id_for_embed returns the stale id and TopicView.new raises on the missing topic, producing a 500 on the embed endpoint. Any embedding site whose imported topic was later deleted serves a 500 from /embed/best with no cleanup mechanism anywhere in the diff.

[BUG] This unrelated migration edit adds `force: true` to create_table, which drops any existing top_topics table before recreating it. Any site that already ran the original migration (or where the top_topics data exists) has its top_topics rows silently destroyed on the next migration run; also the change is not traceable to the embed feature at all.

[ADVISORY] The PR removes the `--category` CLI option and category lookup from the Disqus import task, silently replacing them with TopicEmbed.import_remote, which has no category support. Existing operators running the documented `disqus:import -c <category>` workflow get an 'unknown option' failure or topics created in the default category with no way to set one; this is unrelated scope drift bundled into an embed PR.

[ADVISORY] The retrieve path enqueues a job that can permanently fail (invalid host, missing embed_by_username user, unreadable page), but the loading view's only client behavior is a 30-second reload loop, so the design never surfaces failure. A visitor to a page whose embed URL cannot be retrieved gets a 'Loading Discussion...' page that reloads every 30 seconds forever, hammering the server and never telling the site owner anything failed; the spec coverage only tests the enqueue path, not any failure terminal state.

[ADVISORY] The update branch assumes `embed.post` is always present, but nothing in the diff enforces that invariant (no validation, no handling of deleted posts), so `PostRevisor.new(post)` receives nil when the referenced post has been deleted. Once a feed item's post is deleted (leaving the TopicEmbed row behind), every hourly PollFeed run crashes with NoMethodError on nil, and because PollFeed has `retry: false` the entire remaining feed is skipped each cycle.

[ADVISORY] The `feed_key` method (commented as the modified-detection cache key) is defined but never called anywhere in the diff, so the declared deduplication mechanism is dead code. Feed polling re-imports and re-revises every item on every run with only the content_sha1 check as a backstop; the next maintainer reading `feed_key` will assume conditional fetching exists when it does not — an implementation stub not traceable to the stated behavior.

[ADVISORY] The RSS/ATOM feed polling subsystem (new gems, scheduled job, three site settings, an admin 'Embedding' settings tab) is a whole second feature that goes beyond 'embed URL handling and validation', and it is wired into the embed retrieve path (TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve calls Jobs::PollFeed synchronously). A user hitting /embed/best for an un-imported page triggers a full feed download and synchronous import of every feed item inside their background job, coupling the embed endpoint's latency and failure modes to feed health; if this feature is not in the stated requirements it should be split out.

[BUG] Post#cook returns `raw` verbatim for cook_method raw_html, and TopicEmbed.import feeds unsanitized external RSS/scraped HTML through this path, so the entire sanitization pipeline is bypassed for imported content. Any HTML/JS in a polled feed or scraped page is stored as-is in `cooked` and rendered with `raw post.cooked` in embed/best.html.erb (and on the main forum topic), giving an external feed author stored XSS against every visitor of the embed page; the imported-content trust boundary is inverted.

[BUG] The template closes the header conditional with `<%- end if %>`, which compiles to the Ruby fragment `end if ` — a syntax error (modifier `if` with no condition). ActionView raises a SyntaxError compiling embed/best whenever the topic-view branch renders, so the embed endpoint 500s even after a topic is successfully imported, leaving every embed permanently on the loading/reload page.

[BUG] poll_feed reads `i.content.scrub` unconditionally, but SimpleRSS only maps `content` for Atom feeds — RSS 2.0 items expose `description` and no `content`, so `i.content` is nil. For an RSS (non-Atom) feed the scheduled job dies with NoMethodError on nil.scrub on the first item; with `sidekiq_options retry: false` the import silently never runs again, so the entire feed feature is dead for the majority of feeds.

[ADVISORY] TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously inside the RetrieveTopic background job, which re-downloads and re-imports the entire RSS feed on every embed miss. One anonymous page view of a not-yet-imported article triggers a full-feed fetch plus N TopicEmbed lookups/imports; a popular blog page with no topic yet turns each 60-second throttle window into a full-feed poll, hammering the publisher's server and the Discourse DB from web traffic; the shape should be an enqueue plus a targeted fetch, not a synchronous full poll per request.

[ADVISORY] `feed_key` ("feed-modified:...") is defined but never read or written anywhere in the diff, so the conditional-fetch caching it implies does not exist. The hourly job re-fetches and re-hashes the whole feed every run with no If-Modified-Since/ETag support; the dead method misleads the next maintainer into believing modification-based skipping is implemented.

[ADVISORY] poll_feed runs `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` plus a SHA1/full import attempt inside a loop over every feed item — an N+1 query pattern over an unbounded collection. A feed with hundreds of items issues hundreds of individual lookups and up to hundreds of PostCreator/topic transactions inside one Sidekiq job with no batching (a single IN/join lookup would serve the membership test), so runtime grows linearly with feed size on the hottest path of the feature and a large feed stalls the hourly job.

[ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import does check-then-insert (`where(embed_url: url).first` then `create!`) with no rescue of RecordNotUnique and the update path reads embed.post without a nil check. Two concurrent RetrieveTopic jobs for the same embed_url race past the SELECT, one loses on the unique index and the whole transaction raises into Sidekiq; separately, an embed row whose post_id no longer resolves (no FK exists to prevent it) makes the update branch call PostRevisor.new(nil) and the job dies with NoMethodError on every poll run.

[ADVISORY] The controller enqueues a RetrieveTopic job on every request where no topic exists yet; the 60-second throttle lives inside the job, not at enqueue time. A heavily-viewed embedding page that fails to import (invalid host, feed disabled, embed_by_username unset) enqueues one Sidekiq job per page view forever — thousands of no-op jobs that each burn a Redis throttle check — a queue-flooding path with no enqueue-side guard.

[ADVISORY] The referer gate compares `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` with exact string equality, but URI#host preserves the case the browser sent while SiteSetting is free-text admin input. An admin who enters embeddable_host as "EvilTrout.com" (or any mixed case) blocks every embed request with 403, since browsers lower-case the Referer host; the write path (settings UI) and the compare path disagree on canonical form with no normalization on either side.

[ADVISORY] `force: true` was added to the already-released CreateTopTopics migration, converting a no-op into a destructive DROP+CREATE on any environment where the migration re-runs (db:migrate:redo, db:rollback step-through, multi-instance bootstraps). Any redo/rollback path silently drops all top_topics rows; the same `force: true` in the new topic_embeds migration masks schema drift instead of surfacing it. The change exists to make specs pass, not for production safety.

[ADVISORY] topic_id and post_id are plain integer columns with NOT NULL but no foreign keys and no index on topic_id, while TopicEmbed.import dereferences embed.post on the update path. A topic or post deleted through normal Discourse moderation leaves a dangling topic_embeds row with no DB-enforced integrity; topic_id_for_embed keeps returning the dead topic_id, TopicView.new 500s the embed endpoint, and the update branch calls PostRevisor on a post that no longer exists.

[ADVISORY] The loading view unconditionally reloads the iframe after a bare literal 30000 ms, with no failure signal from the import job and no retry cap. When import permanently fails (invalid host, feed disabled, user missing), every visitor's browser reloads the embed endpoint every 30 seconds indefinitely — an unbounded client-side poll loop whose 30-second provenance/unit is unexpressed and whose failure case has no terminal state.

[ADVISORY] The Disqus import was rewired through TopicEmbed.import_remote, silently dropping two behaviors of the previous path: the `--category/-c` CLI option was removed, and `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` is no longer passed, so imported topics are timestamped with import time. Operators running the documented `-c` flag get an unrecognized-option failure (or silently ignored option on some Thor versions), and all imported threads land in the default category with wrong dates — a contract break for existing import scripts whose data (chronological ordering, category placement) changes silently.

[ADVISORY] The posts loop renders `post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username` per post, but the controller constructs TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5}) with no explicit eager loading of users. Each of the up-to-5 best posts triggers a separate user lookup (and post.url lookups) per embed render; on a page embedded across many articles this multiplies into thousands of extra queries per hour for content that never changes between the 1-minute cache expiries.

[BUG] PollFeed imports raw RSS item content with zero HTML sanitization, and that content is later served unsanitized from the Discourse origin. `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` passes attacker-controlled feed HTML straight into TopicEmbed.import, which stores it with cook_method raw_html (post.cook returns raw verbatim), and embed/best.html.erb line 19 renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. A malicious or compromised feed lets arbitrary <script> execute in the iframe under the Discourse site's origin — stored XSS against every visitor of an embedded page, and the imported topic is also visible in the main forum.

[BUG] The `imported_from` footer interpolates `url` directly into an HTML attribute without escaping, so a feed-supplied URL containing a single quote breaks out of the href attribute. `contents << "... #{url}"` — the URL only has to start with http(s)://, so a feed entry with link `http://x/' onmouseover='alert(1)` injects attributes/HTML into the raw_html post rendered with `raw`. Every feed-driven import path (poll_feed, retrieve_topic, disqus.thor) hits this.

[ADVISORY] The postMessage origin check uses substring matching, not an exact origin comparison. `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any origin that is a substring of the configured discourseUrl — e.g. with discourseUrl `http://discourse.example.com`, a page at origin `http://discourse.example` (or any attacker controlling a domain that is a prefix of it) can drive iframe sizing. Should compare against an exact origin (e.g. a dedicated discourseOrigin variable).

[ADVISORY] `request.referer` is interpolated into the layout's inline JavaScript as the postMessage targetOrigin without escaping or validation. A Referer header containing `'` or `)` from the (host-checked) embedding page breaks out of the JS string literal in the embed layout, causing a JS syntax error (resize messages never sent, embed collapses to default height) — and the raw interpolation invites script injection the moment the referer check is loosened. Should use `j`/json_escape or window.location.origin.

[ADVISORY] The update path assumes `embed.post` exists, crashing with NoMethodError when the referenced post was deleted. PollFeed runs hourly; if an embedded topic's post is deleted (moderator action, user deletion) while the topic_embed row remains, `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!!` raises NoMethodError, and since PollFeed is scheduled with `retry: false` the entire feed poll silently dies at that item every hour, freezing all subsequent imports.

[ADVISORY] `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` has no exception handling for fetch/parse failures, and the job sets `retry: false`. A transient network failure or malformed feed response on the hourly poll raises out of execute and is swallowed (retry disabled), so feed import stalls until the next hour with no logging, error notification, or backoff; the operator cannot distinguish 'feed unchanged' from 'poller broken'.

[ADVISORY] The loading view unconditionally reloads the parent document location every 30 seconds with no failure terminal state. When RetrieveTopic rejects the URL (invalid_host?, embeddable_host mismatch, missing embed_by_username user), the embed page reloads forever in a 30-second loop, and because the job path is throttled per-URL via redis for 60s, each reload re-enqueues a job — a popular page left misconfigured burns Sidekiq jobs indefinitely while visitors see an eternal 'Loading Discussion...'.

[ADVISORY] absolutize_urls only rewrites hrefs/srcs that start with a literal `/`, so relative references like `foo/page.html` or `../img/x.jpg` in feed content remain relative. When the embedded iframe is served from the Discourse host, those unresolved relative URLs resolve against Discourse, producing broken links/images in every imported article that uses non-root-relative URLs — the next maintainer extending this has no single place to fix path handling because the logic is hand-inlined for two tag names.

[ADVISORY] An unrelated, previously-committed migration was retroactively changed to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, which drops the table if it already exists. Any environment where this migration is replayed (multi-DB setups, bin/rake db:migrate:redo, restore pipelines) silently destroys all TopTopic period counters, and changing an already-released migration means existing databases never get the altered behavior — the edit is pure risk with no benefit in this PR.

[ADVISORY] A unique index on embed_url plus a non-atomic check-then-create means two concurrent RetrieveTopic jobs for the same URL race and one crashes the transaction with ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique. The 60-second redis throttle only guards same-process requests; two different visitors hitting /embed/best on different servers within the job queue window both enqueue retrieve_topic, both find no TopicEmbed, both attempt PostCreator + TopicEmbed.create!, and the loser's job raises RecordNotUnique (unhandled, job fails with retry noise). A rescue-and-retry/refind of the embed row is needed.

[BUG] Imported RSS/scraped content is stored and rendered as unsanitized raw HTML, creating a stored XSS pipeline into every page the embed is displayed on. TopicEmbed.import passes feed/scrape contents to PostCreator with cook_method raw_html, Post#cook then `return raw` (app/models/post.rb:131) skipping the entire sanitizing cooking pipeline, and embed/best.html.erb renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (line 17). An attacker who controls or compromises the polled RSS feed, or the page at any URL on embeddable_host, injects `<script>` that executes on the Discourse origin (cookies, CSRF, admin actions) for every visitor to the embedding site and the forum topic.

[BUG] The embed_url is string-interpolated into an HTML anchor without escaping, allowing attribute breakout inside raw-cooked post content. `contents << "\n
\n... #{url}"` — the only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which still permits `'` and `>` (e.g. `http://x/' onclick='...` or `http://x/'>

[BUG] request.referer is interpolated unescaped into an inline JavaScript string, yielding reflected XSS via a crafted Referer header. `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` — a Referer containing `'});alert(1);//` or `</script>` closes the JS string/script tag and executes attacker JS in the embed page's Discourse origin; the referer is fully attacker-controlled header text and the ERB `<%= %>` does not escape quotes inside a script context.

[BUG] The ensure_embeddable access control gates on the client-supplied Referer header, so the check provides no real authorization boundary. request.referer is an attacker-set header on any direct HTTP request, so anyone (not just the trusted embeddable host) can call /embed/best and trigger topic retrieval/content import jobs for arbitrary embed_urls on the embeddable host; combined with the unconditional `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` this also exposes the embedded discussion page to clickjacking from any site, defeating frame-busting for this route.

[ADVISORY] open-uri follows HTTP redirects, so the embeddable_host URL check is bypassable via a redirect to an internal address (SSRF). invalid_host? validates only the initial URI host, then TopicEmbed.import_remote calls `open(url).read` — open-uri transparently follows 3xx redirects, so a page on embeddable_host (or a compromised/open-redirect endpoint on it) redirects to http://169.254.169.254/ or an internal service and the server fetches and imports that response. Staff-flagged no_throttle requests amplify this per-request.

[ADVISORY] The postMessage origin check uses substring matching (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`), which accepts any origin string that appears anywhere in the Discourse URL. e.g. an origin equal to any prefix/substring of discourseUrl (or a crafted origin matching an embedded portion of the URL string) passes the check, letting a malicious page that gets the embed script loaded manipulate the iframe height; impact is limited to layout distortion (UI redressing aid) because the only message handled is resize.

[ADVISORY] An attacker-triggerable background job runs a full feed poll synchronously (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`) with retry disabled and no per-caller cost bound, enabling resource-exhaustion amplification of the unauthenticated /embed/best endpoint. Anyone who spoofs the Referer header can enqueue RetrieveTopic jobs at will (the 60s Redis throttle is keyed per embed_url, so varying embed_urls on the embeddable host defeats it), each of which fetches remote content, runs Nokogiri/readability parsing, and potentially a full feed poll and topic creation — flooding sidekiq and creating attacker-chosen topics as the configured embed_by_username user.

[BUG] The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' tests pass for the wrong reason: they never stub SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?, which defaults to false in the test environment, so poll_feed is skipped by the first condition regardless of the setting under test. These tests verify nothing about the feed_polling_url/embed_by_username guards; if those guards were deleted from Jobs::PollFeed#execute (spec lines 13-15 of app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), both tests would still pass, giving false confidence that the enqueue-gating logic is covered.

[BUG] The 'tells the topic retriever to work' test asserts TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve is called, but EmbedController#best (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb line 15) never calls TopicRetriever — it calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...); the spec verifies a mock contract that does not exist in the code under test. If Jobs.enqueue is not inline in the test environment, this test fails or (with inline jobs) exercises the real RetrieveTopic job path — which calls TopicEmbed.import_remote and performs open(url) against the network — rather than verifying the controller's actual enqueue call; a regression that changes the enqueued job name or its arguments (user_id, embed_url) goes undetected because the test asserts the wrong collaborator entirely.

[BUG] The 'is 404 without an embed_url' test cannot verify what it claims: params.require(:embed_url) in EmbedController#best raises ActionController::ParameterMissing, which in a Rails controller spec propagates as an exception rather than producing a 404 response, so the test either errors or, at best, never asserts the specific 404 status named in its description. The test asserts only response.should_not be_success with no status-code check, so any failure mode (500, 302, 403) passes; the promised-404 behavior of the endpoint is unverified and the spec's own name is a false claim about what is tested.

[ADVISORY] Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed — the entire new behavior in this diff (SimpleRSS parsing, the link/id fallback regex, CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), and delegation to TopicEmbed.import per item, app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb lines 21-37) — has zero coverage; the only test that reaches it stubs poll_feed itself. Checked spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb, spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb — none exercises poll_feed's body. The ATOM fallback (url = i.id when link is missing/non-http) and the content-scrub path will break silently in production feeds (e.g. an item with a blank link raises NoMethodError on i.content.scrub for ATOM feeds lacking content) with no test to catch it.

[ADVISORY] The 'raises an error with a missing host' and 'raises an error with no referer' tests assert only response.should_not be_success, never that the status is the 403 that Discourse::InvalidAccess produces. An operator diagnosing a misconfigured embeddable_host gets no protection against a 500-class regression here: if the controller began raising an unhandled error (e.g. the rescue URI::InvalidURIError in ensure_embeddable is removed or misplaced relative to the raise), these tests still pass because any non-2xx satisfies the assertion, masking a crash as an intended access denial.

[ADVISORY] The 'Supports updating the post' test asserts only post.cooked =~ /new contents/ and never verifies the content_sha1 bookkeeping (embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...)) or that a re-import with unchanged contents skips the revision, which is the core idempotency contract of TopicEmbed.import's update branch (app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 30-35). If the content_sha1 comparison were broken (e.g. always unequal, causing PostRevisor to fire and re-notify watchers on every hourly poll), this test still passes because it only covers the changed-content path; a feed polled hourly would silently revise every topic every hour and no spec would fail.

[ADVISORY] The 'creates a topic view when a topic_id is found' test stubs TopicView.new entirely, so the actual rendering path of the embed feature (app/views/embed/best.html.erb iterating @topic_view.posts, and the loading template branch) is never exercised by any test in the diff. Checked spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb and spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb — neither renders the view; a nil post.user or missing topic in best.html.erb (post.user.small_avatar_url on a deleted user) produces a 500 in every embedded page and no test catches it because TopicView.new is mocked out and render is never asserted.

[BUG] force: true was added to the already-shipped CreateTopTopics migration, making it destructive on re-run. Any environment that re-runs this migration (db:migrate:redo, a dev/staging DB where the migration is still pending but the top_topics table already exists from an earlier checkout, or a fresh clone where schema was loaded then migrations run) silently DROPs the existing top_topics table along with all period/counts data for every topic, which is unrecoverable without a backup.

[BUG] create_table :topic_embeds, force: true on a table with null: false topic_id/post_id columns drops any pre-existing topic_embeds table on re-run. If this migration is ever re-run (db:migrate:redo, or a partially-migrated environment where the table already exists with imported topic/post associations), all topic_embed rows are silently dropped, orphaning every imported topic from its source URL so feed polling re-imports duplicates and embed lookups 404.

[BUG] On the update path, embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1) runs unconditionally after PostRevisor#revise!, without checking whether the revision actually succeeded. PostRevisor#revise! returns false without saving when should_revise? is false, and the new @post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]) can still fail on a DB error or a revision being blocked (e.g. editing window / staff constraints); when that happens the stored content_sha1 is advanced anyway, so every subsequent poll of the RSS feed computes a matching sha1, skips the revise, and the post's content is never updated — the article update is silently lost forever.

On the supported Ruby version, every feed poll raises NoMethodError (undefined method `scrub' for String) after the network fetch succeeds, so feed importing never works and the hourly job fails on every run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The `best` action calls `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` but when `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), ...)` runs with an anonymous visitor (current_user nil), the enqueued job's `args[:user_id]` is nil, and RetrieveTopic then calls `TopicRetriever.new(embed_url, no_throttle: user.try(:staff?))` with `no_throttle: nil`, so the throttle applies — fine — but the controller renders 'loading' with no @topic_view while the loading view's layout postMessage targets `<%= request.referer %>` which is nil when the referer was absent, emitting `parent.postMessage(..., '')`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` executes the entire feed poll synchronously inside the retrieve_topic sidekiq job, but PollFeed's execute guard re-checks `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` — already true — and `poll_feed` then does a blocking `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` network fetch plus a PostCreator DB write per item, all inside a job whose sole purpose is to fetch one URL. Each first-time embed request triggers a full-feed import inside the retrieve_topic worker; a large feed makes the worker block for minutes and hammers the third-party feed server on every new embedded URL, and if the feed fetch raises (e.g. timeout) the RetrieveTopic job fails with retry instead of falling through to fetch_http.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously (no Sidekiq enqueue) before `fetch_http` (lib/topic_retriever.rb). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does a blocking `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all `rss.items`, calling `TopicEmbed.import` per item (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). This means a first-time embed retrieval can trigger a full feed fetch/import unrelated to the single `@embed_url`, creating a significant performance/load/scalability concern and coupling embed retrieval latency to feed size/availability. The finding’s point about exceptions from `open(...)` aborting the flow is also plausible since there’s no rescue around the PollFeed call in `perform_retrieve`, but the diff doesn’t specify intended fallback behavior, making this more of an architecture/robustness concern than a strictly verifiable correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicEmbed.import stores remote feed/retrieved HTML as cooked content with cook_method raw_html, bypassing the sanitizing cook pipeline, and best.html.erb renders it with raw post.cooked, so any script/iframe injected into the source RSS feed or embedded page executes in the Discourse-origin embed iframe. A compromised or malicious embedded site feeds arbitrary HTML through import_remote/PollFeed; it is rendered unsanitized at /embed/best, giving an attacker script execution in the forum's origin (cookie/CSRF theft) — the normal cook pipeline's sanitization is the control this diff explicitly skips.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a `cook_method` of `:raw_html` (Post.cook_methods) and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (which is typically where sanitization would occur). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and supplies HTML content from RSS (`Jobs::PollFeed` uses `i.content`/`CGI.unescapeHTML`) or remote fetch (`TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses `open(url).read`). The embed view `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders `raw post.cooked`, so any HTML stored will be emitted unescaped into `/embed/best` under the Discourse origin. This makes injection of `<script>`/dangerous HTML from the feed/remote page a real XSS risk in the embedded iframe, consistent with the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] poll_feed calls CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) and SimpleRSS returns nil for tags absent from an RSS item (RSS items have description, not content), so every poll of a plain RSS feed raises NoMethodError on nil.scrub and no item is ever imported. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The PR removes the `--category` CLI option and category lookup from the Disqus import task, silently replacing them with TopicEmbed.import_remote, which has no category support. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The retrieve path enqueues a job that can permanently fail (invalid host, missing embed_by_username user, unreadable page), but the loading view's only client behavior is a 30-second reload loop, so the design never surfaces failure. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The update branch assumes `embed.post` is always present, but nothing in the diff enforces that invariant (no validation, no handling of deleted posts), so `PostRevisor.new(post)` receives nil when the referenced post has been deleted. If the referenced post has been deleted, `embed.post` will be `nil` even though `topic_embeds.post_id` is non-null, and nothing in the diff validates presence of the associated post or handles `nil`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `feed_key` method (commented as the modified-detection cache key) is defined but never called anywhere in the diff, so the declared deduplication mechanism is dead code. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The RSS/ATOM feed polling subsystem (new gems, scheduled job, three site settings, an admin 'Embedding' settings tab) is a whole second feature that goes beyond 'embed URL handling and validation', and it is wired into the embed retrieve path (TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve calls Jobs::PollFeed synchronously). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Post#cook returns `raw` verbatim for cook_method raw_html, and TopicEmbed.import feeds unsanitized external RSS/scraped HTML through this path, so the entire sanitization pipeline is bypassed for imported content. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The template closes the header conditional with `<%- end if %>`, which compiles to the Ruby fragment `end if ` — a syntax error (modifier `if` with no condition). adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out the same syntax error: the ERB template incorrectly closes an if block with `end if` (invalid Ruby/ERB) and should use plain `end`, otherwise rendering raises a SyntaxError.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] poll_feed reads `i.content.scrub` unconditionally, but SimpleRSS only maps `content` for Atom feeds — RSS 2.0 items expose `description` and no `content`, so `i.content` is nil. adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same root bug: `i.content.scrub` is called unconditionally, but many RSS (non-Atom) feeds don’t populate `content` (they use `description`), making `i.content` nil and causing a NoMethodError/nil crash. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously inside the RetrieveTopic background job, which re-downloads and re-imports the entire RSS feed on every embed miss. One anonymous page view of a not-yet-imported article triggers a full-feed fetch plus N TopicEmbed lookups/imports; a popular blog page with no topic yet turns each 60-second throttle window into a full-feed poll, hammering the publisher's server and the Discourse DB from web traffic; the shape should be an enqueue plus a targeted fetch, not a synchronous full poll per request.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` synchronously calling `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true (lib/topic_retriever.rb). `TopicRetriever` is invoked from the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` background job (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb), which is enqueued on an embed miss (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` downloads and parses the entire feed and iterates all items (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` then `rss.items.each`), potentially doing many `TopicEmbed.import` operations per miss. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `feed_key` ("feed-modified:...") is defined but never read or written anywhere in the diff, so the conditional-fetch caching it implies does not exist. The hourly job re-fetches and re-hashes the whole feed every run with no If-Modified-Since/ETag support; the dead method misleads the next maintainer into believing modification-based skipping is implemented.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the method `feed_key` computes a Redis key (`"feed-modified:..."`) but is never called anywhere in the diff. The actual polling logic in `poll_feed` always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all items with no ETag/If-Modified-Since or other skip mechanism. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] poll_feed runs `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` plus a SHA1/full import attempt inside a loop over every feed item — an N+1 query pattern over an unbounded collection. A feed with hundreds of items issues hundreds of individual lookups and up to hundreds of PostCreator/topic transactions inside one Sidekiq job with no batching (a single IN/join lookup would serve the membership test), so runtime grows linearly with feed size on the hottest path of the feature and a large feed stalls the hourly job.

This is a diff-grounded linear-scaling/performance concern (N+1 style) rather than a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import does check-then-insert (`where(embed_url: url).first` then `create!`) with no rescue of RecordNotUnique and the update path reads embed.post without a nil check. Two concurrent RetrieveTopic jobs for the same embed_url race past the SELECT, one loses on the unique index and the whole transaction raises into Sidekiq; separately, an embed row whose post_id no longer resolves (no FK exists to prevent it) makes the update branch call PostRevisor.new(nil) and the job dies with NoMethodError on every poll run.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the create path does a check-then-insert (`embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then `TopicEmbed.create!`) while the migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`. With concurrent `RetrieveTopic` jobs for the same `embed_url`, both can pass the `first` check and one will raise on the unique index with no `RecordNotUnique` handling, causing the Sidekiq job to fail. In the update path, `post = embed.post` is used without a nil check and then passed to `PostRevisor.new(post)`; since there is no FK enforcing `post_id` and posts can be deleted, `embed.post` can be nil and this will crash.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The controller enqueues a RetrieveTopic job on every request where no topic exists yet; the 60-second throttle lives inside the job, not at enqueue time. A heavily-viewed embedding page that fails to import (invalid host, feed disabled, embed_by_username unset) enqueues one Sidekiq job per page view forever — thousands of no-op jobs that each burn a Redis throttle check — a queue-flooding path with no enqueue-side guard.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, it unconditionally does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading` (no enqueue-side throttling/guard). The only throttle is inside `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, which runs when the job executes (via `Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute` -> `TopicRetriever#retrieve`), so a high-traffic embed URL with no existing TopicEmbed will enqueue one Sidekiq job per page view. Even if `TopicRetriever` quickly bails (e.g., because it was recently retrieved) it still consumes a job slot and does Redis ops; and if `embed_by_username` is unset, `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` calls `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` which can error, further compounding queue churn. This is a diff-grounded queue-flooding/DoS path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The referer gate compares `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` with exact string equality, but URI#host preserves the case the browser sent while SiteSetting is free-text admin input. An admin who enters embeddable_host as "EvilTrout.com" (or any mixed case) blocks every embed request with 403, since browsers lower-case the Referer host; the write path (settings UI) and the compare path disagree on canonical form with no normalization on either side.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the gate is `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (string `!=`). Hostnames are case-insensitive, but neither side is normalized (e.g., `downcase`/punycode), and `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` is free-text admin input. This can reject valid embed requests if the configured host differs only by case from the Referer host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `force: true` was added to the already-released CreateTopTopics migration, converting a no-op into a destructive DROP+CREATE on any environment where the migration re-runs (db:migrate:redo, db:rollback step-through, multi-instance bootstraps). Any redo/rollback path silently drops all top_topics rows; the same `force: true` in the new topic_embeds migration masks schema drift instead of surfacing it. The change exists to make specs pass, not for production safety.

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table before creating it, so any scenario where the migration is re-run (e.g., `db:migrate:redo`, rolling back and reapplying, or schema re-init paths) can silently delete all `top_topics` rows. The new migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` also uses `force: true`, which likewise would drop/recreate if run against an already-present table, masking drift rather than failing loudly. This is a concrete, diff-grounded destructive behavior change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] topic_id and post_id are plain integer columns with NOT NULL but no foreign keys and no index on topic_id, while TopicEmbed.import dereferences embed.post on the update path. A topic or post deleted through normal Discourse moderation leaves a dangling topic_embeds row with no DB-enforced integrity; topic_id_for_embed keeps returning the dead topic_id, TopicView.new 500s the embed endpoint, and the update branch calls PostRevisor on a post that no longer exists.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `topic_embeds` with `topic_id`/`post_id` as plain NOT NULL integers (migration `20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb`) and only adds a unique index on `embed_url`, with no foreign keys and no `dependent: ...` cleanup in the `TopicEmbed` model. The code then assumes referential integrity: `EmbedController#best` calls `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` (which just plucks `:topic_id`) and immediately does `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` with no existence check; and `TopicEmbed.import`’s update path does `post = embed.post` and then `PostRevisor.new(post)` if content changed. If the associated `topics` or `posts` rows are deleted while a `topic_embeds` row remains, `topic_id_for_embed` can return a dead ID and/or `embed.post` can be nil, leading to exceptions in these call sites. This is a real correctness risk created by the diff’s lack of DB- or model-level integrity enforcement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The loading view unconditionally reloads the iframe after a bare literal 30000 ms, with no failure signal from the import job and no retry cap. When import permanently fails (invalid host, feed disabled, user missing), every visitor's browser reloads the embed endpoint every 30 seconds indefinitely — an unbounded client-side poll loop whose 30-second provenance/unit is unexpressed and whose failure case has no terminal state.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`, the client runs `setTimeout(function() { document.location.reload(); }, 30000);` unconditionally, with no stop condition or retry cap. `EmbedController#best` renders this loading view whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil and enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`. If the background retrieval never creates the embed (e.g., `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` returns early when `embed_by_username` user is missing, or other permanent failures), the iframe will keep re-requesting `/embed/best` every 30s indefinitely, causing perpetual loading and repeated server hits.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The Disqus import was rewired through TopicEmbed.import_remote, silently dropping two behaviors of the previous path: the `--category/-c` CLI option was removed, and `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` is no longer passed, so imported topics are timestamped with import time. adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Thor option `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and deletes the `category_id` lookup/use. It also replaces `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`.import` do not accept or pass `created_at` or `category`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The posts loop renders `post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username` per post, but the controller constructs TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5}) with no explicit eager loading of users. adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `EmbedController#best` creating `@topic_view = TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` and the view rendering `post.user.small_avatar_url`/`post.user.username`, but the diff does not show `TopicView`'s implementation. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] PollFeed imports raw RSS item content with zero HTML sanitization, and that content is later served unsanitized from the Discourse origin. `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` passes attacker-controlled feed HTML straight into TopicEmbed.import, which stores it with cook_method raw_html (post.cook returns raw verbatim), and embed/best.html.erb line 19 renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The `imported_from` footer interpolates `url` directly into an HTML attribute without escaping, so a feed-supplied URL containing a single quote breaks out of the href attribute. `contents << "... #{url}"` — the URL only has to start with http(s)://, so a feed entry with link `http://x/' onmouseover='alert(1)` injects attributes/HTML into the raw_html post rendered with `raw`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The postMessage origin check uses substring matching, not an exact origin comparison. `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any origin that is a substring of the configured discourseUrl — e.g. with discourseUrl `http://discourse.example.com`, a page at origin `http://discourse.example` (or any attacker controlling a domain that is a prefix of it) can drive iframe sizing. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `request.referer` is interpolated into the layout's inline JavaScript as the postMessage targetOrigin without escaping or validation. A Referer header containing `'` or `)` from the (host-checked) embedding page breaks out of the JS string literal in the embed layout, causing a JS syntax error (resize messages never sent, embed collapses to default height) — and the raw interpolation invites script injection the moment the referer check is loosened.
