While it adds extra concerns (escaping/injection) and attributes failure to possible JS syntax errors, it still identifies the core issue: targetOrigin should be an origin, not the full referrer URL, otherwise resizing/postMessage behavior breaks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The update path assumes `embed.post` exists, crashing with NoMethodError when the referenced post was deleted. PollFeed runs hourly; if an embedded topic's post is deleted (moderator action, user deletion) while the topic_embed row remains, `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!!` raises NoMethodError, and since PollFeed is scheduled with `retry: false` the entire feed poll silently dies at that item every hour, freezing all subsequent imports.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally uses it when `content_sha1` changes: `revisor = PostRevisor.new(post)` / `revisor.revise!(...)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). If the associated post has been deleted while the `topic_embeds` row remains (no FK constraints or `dependent: :destroy` shown), `embed.post` will be `nil`, leading to a `NoMethodError` inside `PostRevisor` when it dereferences `@post`. Since `Jobs::PollFeed` is scheduled hourly and iterates `rss.items.each`, an exception would abort the job and prevent processing subsequent items, and `sidekiq_options retry: false` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) means it won't be retried.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` has no exception handling for fetch/parse failures, and the job sets `retry: false`. A transient network failure or malformed feed response on the hourly poll raises out of execute and is swallowed (retry disabled), so feed import stalls until the next hour with no logging, error notification, or backoff; the operator cannot distinguish 'feed unchanged' from 'poller broken'.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no `rescue` around network/IO or parse errors, and the job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`. So a transient fetch error or malformed feed will raise and abort that run, with no in-code handling/logging/notification/backoff. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove it is “swallowed” or “no logging” (Sidekiq typically logs job exceptions), and the job will run again on the next hourly recurrence, so this is more a robustness/operability concern than a definite correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The loading view unconditionally reloads the parent document location every 30 seconds with no failure terminal state. When RetrieveTopic rejects the URL (invalid_host?, embeddable_host mismatch, missing embed_by_username user), the embed page reloads forever in a 30-second loop, and because the job path is throttled per-URL via redis for 60s, each reload re-enqueues a job — a popular page left misconfigured burns Sidekiq jobs indefinitely while visitors see an eternal 'Loading Discussion...'.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` exists it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). The loading template unconditionally reloads itself every 30s with no terminal state (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb). If the background retrieval never creates a `TopicEmbed` (e.g., `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` returns true when `URI(@embed_url).host` != `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, or `fetch_http` bails when `embed_by_username` user is blank), then every reload triggers another enqueue and the user sees an eternal loading loop. Additionally, when `invalid_host?` is true, `retrieved_recently?` is not called (short-circuit in `retrieve`), so there is no redis throttling in that failure mode, exacerbating repeated job enqueues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] absolutize_urls only rewrites hrefs/srcs that start with a literal `/`, so relative references like `foo/page.html` or `../img/x.jpg` in feed content remain relative. When the embedded iframe is served from the Discourse host, those unresolved relative URLs resolve against Discourse, producing broken links/images in every imported article that uses non-root-relative URLs — the next maintainer extending this has no single place to fix path handling because the logic is hand-inlined for two tag names.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` the rewrite only happens when `href`/`src` starts with `'/'` (see `if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')` and the analogous `img` block). Any other valid relative URLs like `foo/page.html` or `../img/x.jpg` are left untouched, and since imported posts are rendered as raw HTML (`cook_method == :raw_html` so `Post#cook` returns `raw`), those relative links/images will resolve against the Discourse origin when displayed in the embed iframe, producing broken resources for such inputs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] An unrelated, previously-committed migration was retroactively changed to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, which drops the table if it already exists. Any environment where this migration is replayed (multi-DB setups, bin/rake db:migrate:redo, restore pipelines) silently destroys all TopTopic period counters, and changing an already-released migration means existing databases never get the altered behavior — the edit is pure risk with no benefit in this PR.

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`, changing `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before recreating it, which can cause silent data loss in scenarios where the migration is replayed (e.g., `db:migrate:redo`, rebuilding from a schema with the table present). This is a real risk introduced by the change and is unrelated to the new embedding/feed features in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] A unique index on embed_url plus a non-atomic check-then-create means two concurrent RetrieveTopic jobs for the same URL race and one crashes the transaction with ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique. The 60-second redis throttle only guards same-process requests; two different visitors hitting /embed/best on different servers within the job queue window both enqueue retrieve_topic, both find no TopicEmbed, both attempt PostCreator + TopicEmbed.create!, and the loser's job raises RecordNotUnique (unhandled, job fails with retry noise). A rescue-and-retry/refind of the embed row is needed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` (migration `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`) but `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` followed by `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction when `embed.blank?`. If two workers concurrently import the same URL (e.g., `Jobs::PollFeed` running while a `RetrieveTopic` job imports, or if `no_throttle` is true), one transaction can hit `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`, and there is no rescue/refind logic in `TopicEmbed.import`/`import_remote`/jobs to handle that gracefully. The finding’s claim that the Redis throttle is only “same-process” is not supported (it uses `$redis.setnx`, which is cross-process), but the underlying check-then-create + unique index race and unhandled `RecordNotUnique` is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Imported RSS/scraped content is stored and rendered as unsanitized raw HTML, creating a stored XSS pipeline into every page the embed is displayed on. TopicEmbed.import passes feed/scrape contents to PostCreator with cook_method raw_html, Post#cook then `return raw` (app/models/post.rb:131) skipping the entire sanitizing cooking pipeline, and embed/best.html.erb renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (line 17). An attacker who controls or compromises the polled RSS feed, or the page at any URL on embeddable_host, injects `<script>` that executes on the Discourse origin (cookies, CSRF, admin actions) for every visitor to the embedding site and the forum topic.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a path where imported content is rendered as raw HTML without passing through the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` feeds `contents` (from RSS in `Jobs::PollFeed` or from `Readability::Document` in `import_remote`) into `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `Post#cook` then short-circuits with `return raw if cook_method == ...[:raw_html]`, skipping the usual rendering/filtering. Finally, `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` outputs it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, and since `post.cooked == post.raw` for `raw_html`, any embedded scripts/unsafe attributes from the feed/page will be stored and executed for viewers of the embed. The diff shows no sanitization step applied to `contents` beyond URL absolutization and `CGI.unescapeHTML(...scrub)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text:
[BUG] The embed_url is string-interpolated into an HTML anchor without escaping, allowing attribute breakout inside raw-cooked post content. `contents << "\n
\n... #{url}"` — the only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which still permits `'` and `>` (e.g. `http://x/' onclick='...` or `http://x/'>

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the unescaped `url` is interpolated directly into an HTML attribute and element text: `"#{url}"` (within `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', ...)`). The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes/`>` etc. The post is then created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for `raw_html`, and `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. This makes crafted feed URLs capable of injecting arbitrary markup/JS into stored content and the embed output.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] request.referer is interpolated unescaped into an inline JavaScript string, yielding reflected XSS via a crafted Referer header. `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` — a Referer containing `'});alert(1);//` or `</script>` closes the JS string/script tag and executes attacker JS in the embed page's Discourse origin; the referer is fully attacker-controlled header text and the ERB `<%= %>` does not escape quotes inside a script context.
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue describes `request.referer` being interpolated directly into inline JavaScript without proper escaping, enabling reflected XSS via a crafted Referer header. This is the same underlying vulnerability as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The ensure_embeddable access control gates on the client-supplied Referer header, so the check provides no real authorization boundary. request.referer is an attacker-set header on any direct HTTP request, so anyone (not just the trusted embeddable host) can call /embed/best and trigger topic retrieval/content import jobs for arbitrary embed_urls on the embeddable host; combined with the unconditional `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` this also exposes the embedded discussion page to clickjacking from any site, defeating frame-busting for this route.
matched_golden_ids: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core problems: using the client-supplied Referer header as a security gate (easily spoofed/bypassable) and setting `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL`, which disables clickjacking protection. While it doesn’t explicitly mention the nil-referer fallback to empty string masking failures, it captures the main underlying issue described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] open-uri follows HTTP redirects, so the embeddable_host URL check is bypassable via a redirect to an internal address (SSRF). invalid_host? validates only the initial URI host, then TopicEmbed.import_remote calls `open(url).read` — open-uri transparently follows 3xx redirects, so a page on embeddable_host (or a compromised/open-redirect endpoint on it) redirects to http://169.254.169.254/ or an internal service and the server fetches and imports that response. Staff-flagged no_throttle requests amplify this per-request.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` which validates only the host of the initially-supplied `@embed_url` via `URI(@embed_url).host` (lib/topic_retriever.rb). If valid, it calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)` (lib/topic_retriever.rb), and `import_remote` fetches the URL content with `open(url).read` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). The diff contains no restriction on redirect targets or re-validation of the final resolved URL host/IP after redirects. Since `open-uri` can follow HTTP redirects, an allowed `embeddable_host` URL that 3xx-redirects to an internal address would be fetched by the server, enabling SSRF. This is a concrete security defect introduced by the new embedding/import functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The postMessage origin check uses substring matching (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`), which accepts any origin string that appears anywhere in the Discourse URL. e.g. an origin equal to any prefix/substring of discourseUrl (or a crafted origin matching an embedded portion of the URL string) passes the check, letting a malicious page that gets the embed script loaded manipulate the iframe height; impact is limited to layout distortion (UI redressing aid) because the only message handled is resize.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the message handler validates the sender with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, which is substring matching rather than an origin equality check. Because `discourseUrl` is a free-form string (set by the embedding page), it can contain an attacker origin as a substring while still producing an iframe URL that loads the real Discourse host (e.g., via URL userinfo like `https://attacker.com@discourse.example/`). In that case, the embedding page’s own `postMessage` events (with `e.origin` == attacker origin) would pass the check and can drive `iframe.height` via `discourse-resize` messages.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] An attacker-triggerable background job runs a full feed poll synchronously (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`) with retry disabled and no per-caller cost bound, enabling resource-exhaustion amplification of the unauthenticated /embed/best endpoint. Anyone who spoofs the Referer header can enqueue RetrieveTopic jobs at will (the 60s Redis throttle is keyed per embed_url, so varying embed_urls on the embeddable host defeats it), each of which fetches remote content, runs Nokogiri/readability parsing, and potentially a full feed poll and topic creation — flooding sidekiq and creating attacker-chosen topics as the configured embed_by_username user.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes /embed/best enqueue `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` when no existing embed is found (EmbedController#best). Access is gated only by `ensure_embeddable`, which checks `request.referer` host against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`—a header a client can spoof. The enqueued job runs `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, whose throttle is keyed solely by `@embed_url` (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so varying paths on the allowed host bypasses the 60s throttle. In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, if `feed_polling_enabled?` it synchronously executes a full feed poll (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`), which fetches/parses remote feed content and imports every item into topics (`rss.items.each ... TopicEmbed.import`). Otherwise it fetches remote content via `open(url).read` + Readability/Nokogiri parsing and can create/update topics as `embed_by_username` (`fetch_http` -> `TopicEmbed.import_remote`). This combination enables attacker-triggerable resource exhaustion and attacker-chosen topic creation on the configured embeddable host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' tests pass for the wrong reason: they never stub SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?, which defaults to false in the test environment, so poll_feed is skipped by the first condition regardless of the setting under test. These tests verify nothing about the feed_polling_url/embed_by_username guards; if those guards were deleted from Jobs::PollFeed#execute (spec lines 13-15 of app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), both tests would still pass, giving false confidence that the enqueue-gating logic is covered.

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#execute, poll_feed is gated by three conditions: feed_polling_enabled?, feed_polling_url.present?, and embed_by_username.present? (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb lines 13-15). In the specs "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username", only feed_polling_url/embed_by_username are stubbed to nil, but feed_polling_enabled? is not stubbed to true (spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb). Since the default setting in site_settings.yml is false for feed_polling_enabled, execute can skip poll_feed due to the first condition, making these tests pass even if the url/username guards were removed. This is a real, diff-grounded test-coverage issue, not a production behavior bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 'tells the topic retriever to work' test asserts TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve is called, but EmbedController#best (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb line 15) never calls TopicRetriever — it calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...); the spec verifies a mock contract that does not exist in the code under test. If Jobs.enqueue is not inline in the test environment, this test fails or (with inline jobs) exercises the real RetrieveTopic job path — which calls TopicEmbed.import_remote and performs open(url) against the network — rather than verifying the controller's actual enqueue call; a regression that changes the enqueued job name or its arguments (user_id, embed_url) goes undetected because the test asserts the wrong collaborator entirely.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows EmbedController#best enqueues a job when no embed exists: `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: embed_url)` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). It never instantiates or calls `TopicRetriever`. However, the new controller spec `"tells the topic retriever to work when no previous embed is found"` expects `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve` to be invoked. This expectation cannot be satisfied by the controller code and will cause the test to fail (and it also wouldn’t detect regressions in the enqueued job name/args).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 'is 404 without an embed_url' test cannot verify what it claims: params.require(:embed_url) in EmbedController#best raises ActionController::ParameterMissing, which in a Rails controller spec propagates as an exception rather than producing a 404 response, so the test either errors or, at best, never asserts the specific 404 status named in its description. The test asserts only response.should_not be_success with no status-code check, so any failure mode (500, 302, 403) passes; the promised-404 behavior of the endpoint is unverified and the spec's own name is a false claim about what is tested.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the first line is `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)`, which will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` when the param is absent. The spec `it "is 404 without an embed_url" do; get :best; response.should_not be_success; end` neither asserts a 404 status nor any specific error handling, so its description (“is 404”) is unverified/misleading and would pass for many non-success outcomes (e.g., 400/403/500/redirect). Whether the exception propagates in this test harness can’t be proven from the diff alone, but the mismatch between the claimed 404 and the actual assertion is directly shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed — the entire new behavior in this diff (SimpleRSS parsing, the link/id fallback regex, CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), and delegation to TopicEmbed.import per item, app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb lines 21-37) — has zero coverage; the only test that reaches it stubs poll_feed itself. Checked spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb, spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb — none exercises poll_feed's body. The ATOM fallback (url = i.id when link is missing/non-http) and the content-scrub path will break silently in production feeds (e.g. an item with a blank link raises NoMethodError on i.content.scrub for ATOM feeds lacking content) with no test to catch it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial logic in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb#poll_feed` (SimpleRSS parsing via `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`, `url = i.id` fallback, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and `TopicEmbed.import(...)` per item). The only added spec (`spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`) asserts that `execute` delegates to `poll_feed` but explicitly stubs `poll_feed` itself, so none of this new behavior is exercised. Other new specs cover `TopicEmbed.import` and `TopicRetriever`, not the feed parsing loop. This is a specific, diff-grounded testing gap (and the code also appears brittle because `i.content` could be nil, making `i.content.scrub` raise), but the primary verifiable issue is the lack of direct coverage for the newly added logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'raises an error with a missing host' and 'raises an error with no referer' tests assert only response.should_not be_success, never that the status is the 403 that Discourse::InvalidAccess produces. An operator diagnosing a misconfigured embeddable_host gets no protection against a 500-class regression here: if the controller began raising an unhandled error (e.g. the rescue URI::InvalidURIError in ensure_embeddable is removed or misplaced relative to the raise), these tests still pass because any non-2xx satisfies the assertion, masking a crash as an intended access denial.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, the tests "raises an error with a missing host" and "raises an error with no referer" only assert `response.should_not be_success` after `get :best`. That is a weak assertion: it would pass for any non-2xx response, including a 500 caused by an unhandled exception in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` (which raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` and rescues `URI::InvalidURIError`). The finding’s broader point—that these tests don’t pin down the intended failure mode/status—is grounded in the diff. However, the specific claim that the correct status must be 403 is not directly verifiable from this diff alone (status mapping for `Discourse::InvalidAccess` is elsewhere).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'Supports updating the post' test asserts only post.cooked =~ /new contents/ and never verifies the content_sha1 bookkeeping (embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...)) or that a re-import with unchanged contents skips the revision, which is the core idempotency contract of TopicEmbed.import's update branch (app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 30-35). If the content_sha1 comparison were broken (e.g. always unequal, causing PostRevisor to fire and re-notify watchers on every hourly poll), this test still passes because it only covers the changed-content path; a feed polled hourly would silently revise every topic every hour and no spec would fail.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial idempotency logic in TopicEmbed.import: it computes content_sha1 and only calls PostRevisor/update_column when content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1 (app/models/topic_embed.rb, update branch). The new spec "Supports updating the post" only asserts the changed-content path via `post.cooked =~ /new contents/` and does not verify that `embed.content_sha1` is updated nor that a re-import with identical contents skips revision. This is a specific, diff-grounded testing gap rather than a demonstrable defect in the implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'creates a topic view when a topic_id is found' test stubs TopicView.new entirely, so the actual rendering path of the embed feature (app/views/embed/best.html.erb iterating @topic_view.posts, and the loading template branch) is never exercised by any test in the diff. Checked spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb and spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb — neither renders the view; a nil post.user or missing topic in best.html.erb (post.user.small_avatar_url on a deleted user) produces a 500 in every embedded page and no test catches it because TopicView.new is mocked out and render is never asserted.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, the “creates a topic view when a topic_id is found” example fully mocks `TopicView.new` (`TopicView.expects(:new)...`) and the other branch (no topic_id) only asserts the retriever call; neither spec enables `render_views` or asserts rendered templates/content. As a result, the new templates `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` (iterating `@topic_view.posts` and referencing `post.user.small_avatar_url`, etc.) and `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` are not exercised by tests added in this diff. The claimed specific failure mode (deleted/nil user causing 500) is speculative from the diff, but the lack of view-path coverage due to mocking and no render assertions is directly verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] force: true was added to the already-shipped CreateTopTopics migration, making it destructive on re-run. Any environment that re-runs this migration (db:migrate:redo, a dev/staging DB where the migration is still pending but the top_topics table already exists from an earlier checkout, or a fresh clone where schema was loaded then migrations run) silently DROPs the existing top_topics table along with all period/counts data for every topic, which is unrecoverable without a backup.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it. If this already-shipped migration is re-run in any scenario (e.g., `db:migrate:redo`, pending migration but table exists, or running migrations after loading a schema that already contains `top_topics`), it can silently destroy existing `top_topics` data. This is a real, diff-grounded data-loss risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] create_table :topic_embeds, force: true on a table with null: false topic_id/post_id columns drops any pre-existing topic_embeds table on re-run. If this migration is ever re-run (db:migrate:redo, or a partially-migrated environment where the table already exists with imported topic/post associations), all topic_embed rows are silently dropped, orphaning every imported topic from its source URL so feed polling re-imports duplicates and embed lookups 404.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` in `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb`, which *would* drop an existing `topic_embeds` table if this migration were executed against a DB where that table already exists. However, under normal Rails migration semantics, this migration is applied once (tracked in `schema_migrations`), and `db:migrate:redo` rolls back before re-applying, so the described “silent drop on re-run”/data loss scenario requires an abnormal state (e.g., the table exists but the migration is considered pending). This is a real, diff-grounded robustness/data-safety concern, but not a verifiable defect in typical execution flow from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] On the update path, embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1) runs unconditionally after PostRevisor#revise!, without checking whether the revision actually succeeded. PostRevisor#revise! returns false without saving when should_revise? is false, and the new @post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]) can still fail on a DB error or a revision being blocked (e.g. editing window / staff constraints); when that happens the stored content_sha1 is advanced anyway, so every subsequent poll of the RSS feed computes a matching sha1, skips the revise, and the post's content is never updated — the article update is silently lost forever.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import’s update path, when `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`, it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` and then unconditionally does `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` without checking the return value of `revise!` (which the diff shows can return `false` early: `return false if not should_revise?` in `lib/post_revisor.rb`). This can advance `content_sha1` even if the post wasn’t updated, creating a state where future polls think the content matches and skip further updates, leaving the post stale.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The update path dereferences embed.post with no guard for a stale/deleted post_id, and the topic_embeds table has no FK or dependent-destroy to either posts or topics. When the referenced post is deleted (regular Discourse post deletion), PostRevisor.new(post) raises NoMethodError inside the scheduled PollFeed job; with sidekiq_options retry: false the failure is silent, and because content_sha1 is never updated for that URL the job re-raises on every hourly poll — the whole feed import loop stops at that item and later feed entries are never processed.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally instantiates `PostRevisor.new(post)` when `content_sha1` differs (app/models/topic_embed.rb). If the referenced post has been hard-deleted (or otherwise missing), `embed.post` will be `nil` and this will raise. The migration creates `topic_embeds.post_id`/`topic_id` with no foreign keys or cascading cleanup (db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb), and the models have `belongs_to` without `dependent:` options, so orphaned rows are possible. In `Jobs::PollFeed`, a raised exception would abort the `rss.items.each` loop (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), and with `sidekiq_options retry: false` it will not be retried automatically, so subsequent items won’t be processed for that run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import is not concurrency-safe against the unique index on embed_url: two workers (RetrieveTopic job and hourly PollFeed both call it) can pass the where(embed_url:).first check simultaneously and the loser raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique on TopicEmbed.create!. Operators enabling both feed polling and embedding on the same articles get intermittent RecordNotUnique exceptions in the RetrieveTopic sidekiq job right after first embed of a new URL; the job retries from scratch and the user's embed iframe shows the loading page for an extra cycle.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does a non-atomic existence check (`embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`) and then, if blank, creates a new row via `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction. The migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` (`add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`). With two workers calling `TopicEmbed.import` for the same URL concurrently (e.g., scheduled `Jobs::PollFeed` and `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`/`TopicRetriever` calling `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`import`), both can pass the `first` check and one will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` on `create!`. The diff contains no rescue/retry or upsert/locking to make this concurrency-safe.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The RSS import backfill runs PostCreator/PostRevisor with skip_validations: true and raw_html cook_method, bypassing model validations and the cooking pipeline that sanitizes HTML. Junk, whitespace, or oversized feed content is imported straight into posts.cooked verbatim, and any feed whose content is not valid HTML is stored and served raw on the public embed/best route — data-integrity cleanup after a bad feed import requires manually deleting topics, since there is no reverse path from topic_embeds back to validated state.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a `raw_html` cook mode that returns `raw` verbatim (`Post#cook` returns `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`), and the RSS/remote import path sets this mode while also bypassing validations: `PostCreator.new(... skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])` in `TopicEmbed.import`, and updates use `PostRevisor#save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` with `skip_validations: true` in the reimport path. Feed content comes from `Jobs::PollFeed` via `i.content` and is not sanitized before being stored, then is rendered on the public `embed#best` route as `raw post.cooked` (ERB `raw`), so untrusted HTML can be persisted and served without the normal sanitizing cooking pipeline. That’s a concrete security/correctness defect introduced by this change (XSS/vector for bad HTML content).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] add_column :cook_method with default 1 silently reclassifies the interpretation of every existing post row under the new enum Post.cook_methods where :regular maps to 1, coupling the default's correctness to Discourse's Enum base offset with no test in the diff. If Post's Enum were ever changed to start at 0 (or a value inserted before :regular), every pre-existing post would be treated as raw_html and Post#cook would return raw unsanitized markup for all user posts; nothing in this migration or the model pins the mapping, so the schema and code are held together only by convention.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `posts.cook_method` with `default: 1, null: false` (db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb) and defines `Post.cook_methods` via `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` (app/models/post.rb). The chosen default value is implicitly coupled to whatever integer mapping `Enum` assigns (i.e., that `:regular` maps to 1), and the diff does not pin that mapping in the schema/model. While this is not a verifiable defect given the current Enum usage, it is a real maintainability/fragility concern introduced by this change; existing rows will take the default and future Enum ordering/offset changes could reinterpret stored values, impacting `Post#cook` behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no content element (plain RSS feeds expose `description`, not `content`; malformed items omit both), and the exception aborts the whole loop before any later item is imported. Because `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the hourly poll job dies on the first bad item and every item after it is silently dropped — feed import permanently stalls with no error surfaced to the operator until the next poll hits the same item again.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop unconditionally does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` for each `rss.items` entry. If `i.content` is `nil` (e.g., feeds providing `description` instead of `content`, or malformed items), calling `.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError` and abort the entire job before later items are processed. There is no per-item rescue, and the job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so a single bad item can repeatedly kill the hourly poll and prevent subsequent imports.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` performs an unbounded network fetch with no timeout and no response size cap. A hung or slow feed server blocks the scheduled Sidekiq worker indefinitely and an attacker-controlled/huge feed can be downloaded entirely into memory; with retry: false the failure is also never retried or surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added scheduled job `Jobs::PollFeed`, `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) performs an HTTP fetch via `open-uri` with no explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` and no limit on response size. This can tie up the Sidekiq worker on slow/hanging servers and can download arbitrarily large feeds into memory during parsing. The same job also sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so transient network failures won’t be retried.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` performs an unbounded, timeout-less HTTP fetch of the embed URL on the request-serving worker path. A slow or unresponsive embed host (the page being embedded is third-party content) hangs the Sidekiq worker with no timeout, and an arbitrarily large page is read fully into memory with no size cap.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the diff adds `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` (see `app/models/topic_embed.rb`). This performs a full HTTP fetch and reads the entire response body into memory with no size limit, and the code does not set any explicit network timeouts or redirect limits on `open-uri`. This is invoked from background execution paths (`TopicRetriever#fetch_http` called by `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, and also from the Disqus import task), so a slow/large/unresponsive remote page can tie up a Sidekiq worker and/or consume excessive memory. The finding’s note about a "request-serving worker path" is imprecise, but the underlying unbounded fetch/read issue is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When no topic exists, the controller enqueues RetrieveTopic and renders 'loading', but the job's retrieve path silently no-ops on every failure (throttled within 60s, embed_url host mismatch, embed_by_username user missing, fetch error), and loading.html.erb blindly reloads every 30s. A user embedding a URL whose retrieval fails gets an iframe stuck in 'Loading Discussion...' forever — the failure of a user-facing operation is completely invisible, with no error state ever rendered.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no topic exists it always enqueues `:retrieve_topic` and renders `loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb), and `loading.html.erb` unconditionally reloads every 30s. The retrieval path can legitimately no-op without surfacing any error: `TopicRetriever#retrieve` skips `perform_retrieve` when `invalid_host?` is true (embed_url host != `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and the controller does not validate `embed_url` host—only `request.referer`), and `fetch_http` returns immediately if `embed_by_username` user lookup yields blank. In these cases no `TopicEmbed` is created and the iframe will stay on the loading page indefinitely with repeated reloads and no error state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import returns nil without any error or log when PostCreator fails (post.blank?), and raises NoMethodError on `embed.post` when the referenced post was deleted while the TopicEmbed row remains. The Disqus importer and PollFeed silently skip failed imports while treating the overall run as successful, and the deleted-post case crashes the retrieve/poll job with an unhandled exception rather than a logged, recoverable error.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path assumes `embed.post` exists: `post = embed.post` then (if SHA differs) `PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!` are called with no nil-check. If the `topic_embeds` row remains but the referenced `posts` row was deleted, `embed.post` will be `nil` and this will raise (e.g., in `PostRevisor.new(nil)` / subsequent calls), crashing `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` / `Jobs::PollFeed` flows. Also, in the create path, if `PostCreator#create` returns nil, the method simply returns nil without logging/raising (`if post.present? ... end`), so callers like `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` silently skip failed imports.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] perform_retrieve synchronously executes the entire PollFeed job (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`), re-fetching and re-parsing the whole RSS feed, once per each not-yet-embedded URL requested. A site embedding N new pages within an hour triggers N full feed fetches on Sidekiq workers — multiplying outbound load against the feed host and delaying each retrieve job by the full feed parse time.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb` `perform_retrieve` does `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` synchronously does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all items. Since `perform_retrieve` is invoked per `@embed_url` (via `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`), each not-yet-embedded URL can trigger a full feed fetch/parse, multiplying outbound requests and increasing retrieve latency. This is a performance/architecture concern rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `feed_key` is computed (an SHA1 of the feed URL) but never used anywhere — the intended modified-since/etag caching is absent, so this is dead code and the poller re-processes every item every hour. Operators reading the code believe feed polling is keyed/cached; in reality each hourly run re-fetches and re-runs TopicEmbed.import for every feed item, relying entirely on the per-item sha1 comparison — deletion test: removing feed_key and its Digest::SHA1 require changes no behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` computes `"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)}"` and the file `require`s `digest/sha1`, but `feed_key` is never referenced by `execute` or `poll_feed`. The polling logic always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates `rss.items.each` calling `TopicEmbed.import(...)` for every item on each run, with no modified-since/etag or redis-based caching keyed by `feed_key`. Removing `feed_key` (and likely the SHA1 require) would not change behavior per the diff, making this dead/unfinished logic rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The origin check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` rejects valid messages whenever the configured discourseUrl lacks a trailing slash or uses a scheme/port variation (e.g. `https://forum.example.com` vs origin `https://forum.example.com` matches, but any path suffix or trailing-slash mismatch like `http://x/` vs origin `http://x` still passes while a discourseUrl without scheme fails all), and the resize handler does nothing when `e.data.height` is 0 or falsy. Embed sites where the configured discourseUrl string doesn't contain the exact origin substring never receive resize messages, so the iframe stays at its default height and content is clipped — the failure is silent with no console error or user-visible hint.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the origin gate is `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) return;`, which *accepts* common trailing-slash/path differences (e.g., `discourseUrl = "http://x/"` and `e.origin = "http://x"` yields index 0, so it does not reject). The finding’s main claim that missing trailing slash or path suffix causes valid messages to be rejected is not supported by the shown logic. The note about `e.data.height` being falsy (e.g., 0) preventing resize is true (`&& e.data.height`), but that’s not the stated failure mode and isn’t clearly a real defect from the diff alone.
